claims: "TACO" was coined by Financial Times columnist Robert Armstrong.
"TACO" describes a market strategy where investors buy during dips caused by Donald Trump’s tariff threats, assuming he will backtrack, leading to a market rebound.
Yahoo News and NPR say the phrase "TACO" was coined to describe a pattern of behavior regarding tariff negotiations during Trump's administration.
Yahoo News and NPR say "TACO" is often referred to as the "TACO trade".
Markets decline when Trump threatens steep tariffs.
Markets rise when Trump reduces or postpones steep tariffs.
President Trump described the question about the term "TACO" as "nasty", according to The New York Times and Facebook.
President Trump argued his actions are "negotiation," not backing down, according to The New York Times and Facebook.
Facebook and Yahoo News say "TACO" is a shorthand on Wall Street to describe the impact of volatile policy announcements on financial markets.
The New York Times reports that the term "TACO" is distinct from the 2016 campaign phrase "taco trucks on every corner".
